architecture.summary: Canonical domain model and persistent schema for AI Multi-Agent Workflow platform. 23 core entities with explicit relationships, UUID identifiers, PostgreSQL storage with JSONB for flexible attributes, migration scripts, generic CRUD service layer with validation, ER diagram, and API contract documentation.
architecture.style: Modular monolith with relational persistence; domain-driven design; repository pattern for data access; JSONB for extensible attributes; OpenAPI 3.0 for API contracts.
architecture.rationale: PostgreSQL with JSONB provides ACID guarantees for core relationships while allowing flexible attribute storage for evolving agent configurations. The domain model reflects the PRD's 23 entities with explicit ownership boundaries. Repository pattern isolates storage concerns. OpenAPI enables client generation for downstream tasks (workflow editor, orchestration server, agent management).
assumptions: UUIDv7 (time-ordered) for primary keys to aid indexing and debugging
JSONB used for: agent configuration, model parameters, tool policies, memory entries, artifact metadata, audit details
Soft deletes via deleted_at timestamp for auditability
Optimistic locking via version column on mutable entities
Multi-tenancy not required in v1 (single-tenant self-hosted)
verified_facts: PRD defines 23 core entities with Russian descriptions and purposes
Child tasks depend on: workflow JSON schema (t_191fcdcb), orchestration API (t_52732c01), agent/provider APIs (t_cb3ae3dd)
Platform principles: platform-owned orchestration, provider independence, controlled autonomy, independent quality verification
Quality Gates, Contracts, and Audit Events are first-class domain concepts
implementation_sequence: 3. Implement repository base class and per-entity repositories
4. Build generic CRUD service layer with validation (Pydantic v2)
5. Write unit tests for repositories and services (≥80% coverage)
6. Generate ER diagram (Mermaid + PNG via mermaid-cli)
acceptance_criteria: All 23 entities have migrations with PK, FK, indexes, constraints
Repository CRUD operations pass unit tests
Service layer validates required fields, FK integrity, unique constraints
ER diagram renders without errors showing all entities and relationships
Integration tests pass: create/read/update/delete/soft-delete for each entity
JSONB fields queryable via GIN indexes where needed
Migration up/down tested on clean database

components.name: Migration Layer
components.responsibility: Schema versioning, idempotent up/down migrations, seed data
components.implementation_notes: 5 migration files: 001_core_entities.sql (Project, Workspace, Environment, Team), 002_agent_entities.sql (AgentDefinition, AgentInstance, ModelProfile, Provider, ToolPolicy), 003_workflow_entities.sql (WorkflowDefinition, WorkflowVersion, WorkflowRun, Task, TaskAttempt, KanbanBoard, Gate, Contract), 004_runtime_entities.sql (Conversation, Memory, ScheduledJob, Artifact, AuditEvent), 005_indexes_constraints.sql (GIN indexes, partial indexes, triggers)

components.name: Domain Models
components.responsibility: SQLAlchemy 2.0 async declarative models mapping to tables; hybrid properties for computed fields
components.implementation_notes: Each model defines: id (UUIDv7, PK), created_at/updated_at/deleted_at (timestamptz), version (int, optimistic lock), JSONB columns for flexible attrs, relationship() for FK navigation. Enum types for status fields (WorkflowRunStatus, TaskStatus, AgentInstanceState, etc.)

components.name: Repository Layer
components.responsibility: Data access abstraction; CRUD + query methods; transaction management; pagination
components.implementation_notes: BaseRepository[T] with: get(id), list(filters, pagination), create(obj), update(id, patch), delete(id, soft=True), hard_delete(id). Specialized repos add domain queries: WorkflowRepository.get_active_version(), TaskRepository.get_pending_for_agent(), AuditRepository.query_by_correlation_id()

components.name: CRUD Service Layer
components.responsibility: Business validation, cross-entity invariants, DTO ↔ model mapping, event emission
components.implementation_notes: Services: ProjectService, WorkspaceService, AgentService, WorkflowService, TaskService, MemoryService, ArtifactService, ProviderService, AuditService. Each exposes async methods returning Pydantic response models. Validation: unique name per workspace, FK existence, state machine transitions (e.g., WorkflowRun: pending→running→completed/failed), Contract verification before TaskAttempt completion

components.name: API Contract (OpenAPI 3.0)
components.responsibility: REST endpoint definitions, request/response schemas, error models, security schemes
components.implementation_notes: Endpoints grouped by entity: /projects, /workspaces, /environments, /agents/definitions, /agents/instances, /workflows/definitions, /workflows/versions, /workflows/runs, /tasks, /tasks/attempts, /kanban/boards, /gates, /contracts, /conversations, /memory, /jobs, /artifacts, /providers, /model-profiles, /tool-policies, /audit. Standard errors: 400 (validation), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict/optimistic lock), 422 (business rule). Auth: Bearer token (JWT) placeholder.

components.name: ER Diagram Generator
components.responsibility: Produce Mermaid ER diagram and rendered PNG/SVG from live schema
components.implementation_notes: Script queries information_schema for tables, columns, FKs. Outputs Mermaid syntax with: entity boxes (table + key columns), relationship lines (crow's foot), color coding by domain group (Project/Workspace, Agent, Workflow, Runtime, Platform). Saved to docs/er-diagram.mmd and docs/er-diagram.png

interfaces.name: Repository Interface
interfaces.contract: BaseRepository[T] protocol with async CRUD + domain-specific query methods. Return types: Domain Model or None. Exceptions: NotFoundError, IntegrityError, OptimisticLockError.
interfaces.error_behavior: Raise domain exceptions; never return null for get(id) — raise NotFoundError. Transactions managed by caller (service layer).
interfaces.compatibility: Stable within v1; new query methods added as needed without breaking existing signatures.

interfaces.name: Service Layer Interface
interfaces.contract: Async methods accepting/returning Pydantic DTOs (CreateXRequest, UpdateXRequest, XResponse, XListResponse). Validation errors → ValidationError with field-level details. Business rule violations → BusinessRuleError with code/message.
interfaces.error_behavior: Structured error responses per RFC 9457 (Problem Details). All mutations emit domain events for audit/logging.
interfaces.compatibility: DTO schemas versioned via OpenAPI; additive changes only in v1.

interfaces.name: REST API (OpenAPI 3.0)
interfaces.contract: OpenAPI 3.0 document at /openapi.json. JSON request/response. Pagination: cursor-based (after, limit). Filtering: ?filter[field]=value. Sorting: ?sort=-created_at. Includes webhook endpoints for async events.
interfaces.error_behavior: Problem Details (RFC 9457) with type, title, status, detail, instance. Rate limiting: 429 with Retry-After.
interfaces.compatibility: Semantic versioning in URL path (/api/v1/). Breaking changes → new version.

interfaces.name: Workflow Definition JSON Schema
interfaces.contract: JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) defining: nodes (agent_definition_id, model_profile_id, tool_policy_id, config), edges (source_node_id, target_node_id, output_mapping), metadata (version, description). Stored in WorkflowDefinition.definition JSONB and WorkflowVersion.definition_snapshot JSONB.
interfaces.error_behavior: Validation at create/update time via JSON Schema validator (jsonschema library). Invalid graphs rejected with path-specific errors.
interfaces.compatibility: Schema versioned; migrations for definition upgrades handled by WorkflowService.

data_model.migration_strategy: Alembic for versioned migrations. Initial migration (001) creates all tables with PKs, FKs, base indexes. Subsequent migrations add: GIN indexes on JSONB columns (002), partial indexes for soft-delete filtering (003), triggers for updated_at/version increment (004), pgvector extension and embedding index on memories.embedding (005, optional). Down migrations reverse in order. Seed data: default ToolPolicy, global Contracts, system Provider entries.

security: All IDs are UUIDv7 — non-sequential, non-guessable
Secrets in Provider.auth_config and Environment.secrets_ref encrypted at rest (pgcrypto or application-layer)
Row-level security policies for multi-tenancy preparation (v2)
AuditEvent captures all mutations with actor, action, before/after
Soft deletes prevent data loss; hard delete requires admin role
API requires Bearer token (JWT); scopes per entity group
SQL injection prevented via parameterized queries (SQLAlchemy ORM)
performance: UUIDv7 primary keys — time-ordered, reduces B-tree fragmentation
Composite indexes: (project_id, created_at) on high-volume tables (WorkflowRun, Task, TaskAttempt, AuditEvent, Memory)
GIN indexes on JSONB columns queried frequently: AgentDefinition.capabilities, WorkflowDefinition.definition, Memory.value, AuditEvent.changes
Partial indexes: WHERE deleted_at IS NULL on all tables
Pagination via cursor (keyset) not OFFSET for large datasets
Connection pooling: PgBouncer or SQLAlchemy pool (min 5, max 20)
Read replicas for analytics queries (AuditEvent, Memory search)
reliability: Optimistic locking via version column on all mutable entities
Foreign keys enforce referential integrity at DB level
NOT NULL constraints on required fields
Check constraints for enum values (status, gate_type, scope)
Transactional outbox pattern for AuditEvent emission (same transaction as domain change)
Idempotency keys on create endpoints (client-generated UUID)
Durable execution: WorkflowRun state persisted at each transition; TaskAttempt records every agent execution
scalability: Partition AuditEvent by month (native PostgreSQL partitioning)
Memory.embedding uses pgvector HNSW index for similarity search
Horizontal sharding by project_id feasible (single-tenant v1, multi-tenant v2)
Background workers for: scheduled jobs, artifact cleanup, memory expiration
observability: Metrics: request latency (histogram), error rate, DB pool usage, migration version
Traces: OpenTelemetry spans for service methods and DB queries
AuditEvent table is the source of truth for compliance/forensics
maintainability: Repository pattern isolates SQL; services contain business logic
Pydantic v2 schemas as single source of truth for validation + OpenAPI
Migrations reviewed via CI; no manual schema changes
ER diagram auto-generated from schema — never hand-edited
Code generation: SQLAlchemy models → Pydantic DTOs → OpenAPI via fastapi/pydantic

decisions.problem: Choose primary datastore for 23-entity domain model with flexible attributes
decisions.selected_option: PostgreSQL 15+ with JSONB for flexible columns
decisions.rationale: ACID for core relationships (FK, constraints); JSONB for evolving agent configs, tool policies, memory values; mature ecosystem; supports pgvector for embeddings; time-tested for multi-agent systems
decisions.consequences: Operational overhead of PostgreSQL; JSONB queries slower than normalized columns; requires GIN indexes for performance

decisions.problem: Primary key strategy for distributed, traceable entities
decisions.selected_option: UUIDv7 (time-ordered UUID) for all primary keys
decisions.rationale: Globally unique without coordination; time-ordered improves B-tree locality and debugging; sortable by creation time; standard (RFC 9562)
decisions.consequences: 16 bytes vs 8 bytes for BIGINT; requires uuid-ossp or gen_random_uuid(v7) extension; slightly larger indexes

decisions.problem: Handle soft deletes and audit trail uniformly
decisions.selected_option: deleted_at timestamp + version column on all tables; AuditEvent append-only table
decisions.rationale: Soft delete preserves referential integrity and audit history; version enables optimistic locking; AuditEvent provides immutable log with correlation_id for tracing
decisions.consequences: All queries must filter deleted_at IS NULL (partial indexes help); storage growth; version increment on every update

decisions.selected_option: JSONB column with JSON Schema validation at application layer
decisions.rationale: Workflow graphs are inherently flexible (nodes, edges, config); JSONB avoids EAV anti-pattern; JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) provides validation without DB migration per change
decisions.consequences: Validation in application layer (not DB); schema evolution requires migration logic in WorkflowService; querying inside definition requires JSONB operators

decisions.selected_option: Provider entity + ModelProfile entity; ToolPolicy separate; all referenced by AgentDefinition/AgentInstance
decisions.rationale: Decouples provider config (auth, endpoints) from model params (temperature, context) from permissions (tools); enables swap without code change; matches PRD provider independence principle
decisions.consequences: Three-table join for agent runtime config; cached in AgentService for performance

decisions.problem: Memory storage with optional vector similarity
decisions.selected_option: Memory table with JSONB value + optional pgvector embedding column
decisions.rationale: Unified key-value memory with scopes (project/workspace/conversation/agent); pgvector enables semantic search when enabled; embedding column nullable for v1 without pgvector
decisions.consequences: pgvector is optional dependency; HNSW index build time; embedding generation async

decisions.selected_option: OpenAPI 3.0 generated from Pydantic v2 models; semantic versioning in URL (/api/v1/)
decisions.rationale: Single source of truth (Pydantic); automatic client SDK generation; breaking changes isolated to new version path; RFC 9457 error format standardizes error handling
decisions.consequences: Requires discipline: additive changes only in v1; code generation pipeline needed

rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: Lacks ACID transactions across entities; FK enforcement manual; no mature vector search; PRD requires explicit relationships and constraints
Single-writer limitation; no concurrent agent workloads; not production-grade for multi-agent orchestration
Sequential IDs leak entity counts; not merge-friendly across instances; harder to debug (no time info)
Random inserts cause B-tree fragmentation; not sortable by creation time; larger index pages
Complex application logic; referential integrity breaks; audit trail fragmented
Over-engineered for v1; read models add complexity; PRD expects direct CRUD for entities
Workflows are user-defined graphs; schema varies per definition; EAV or excessive joins; JSONB is purpose-built
Violates provider independence; couples auth, params, permissions; cannot swap provider without migrating all agents
Operational complexity; data sync issues; pgvector sufficient for single-tenant v1
Workflow Editor (t_191fcdcb) is web-based; REST+JSON simpler for browser; gRPC added later for inter-service

risks.description: JSONB query performance degrades with large documents or missing indexes
risks.mitigation: GIN indexes on all queried JSONB paths; pg_stat_statements monitoring; document size limits in validation

risks.description: Migration conflicts if multiple developers create migrations concurrently
risks.mitigation: Alembic with linear history; CI enforces single-head; migration review required
Use PostgreSQL pgcrypto with key from env var; rotate via re-encryption script; never log decrypted values

risks.description: Circular dependency: WorkflowRun → Task → AgentInstance → WorkflowRun
risks.mitigation: FKs are nullable where cycle occurs (AgentInstance.workflow_run_id, Task.agent_instance_id); application layer enforces consistency

risks.description: Schema evolution for WorkflowDefinition.definition JSONB without migrations
risks.mitigation: Version field in definition.metadata; WorkflowService handles upgrades on load; JSON Schema per version

risks.description: pgvector extension unavailable in managed PostgreSQL (RDS, Cloud SQL)
risks.mitigation: Embedding column nullable; similarity search degrades to keyword fallback; document as known limitation

risks.description: Optimistic lock contention on high-throughput entities (Task, WorkflowRun)
risks.mitigation: Short transactions; retry with exponential backoff in service layer; monitor version conflict rate
